Question: Which aspects of technology from "Star Trek" (any series) have been realized today, if any?
Answer: There are many aspects of technology that appeared in Star Trek that have been invented in our time but none more famous than the earpiece/Bluetooth In Star Trek, an earpiece was a wireless receiver device used by communications officers, science officers and navigators during the 22nd and 23rd centuries. Earpieces were more commonly used aboard Starfleet vessels. They consisted of several metallic rungs, attached to a virtually transparent lead that was inserted into the user's ear, negating the need for tactile support. To activate the earpiece, the user like Lt. Uhura for example, would tap the earpiece and it could complete a whole host of tasks. The signals they received could be amplified throughout the user's ship, although the devices had no automatic protection that might mute or lower loud transmissions. With the earpiece, Uhura or any other qualified Starfleet officer, could contact foreign ships in space and hail them, signals received through the earpiece could be amplified throughout the user's ship, and the device could analyze and hear incoming messages from space and other vessels. Bluetooth earpieces are so commonplace we barely consider them technology. But when Star Trek introduced Lieutenant Uhura’s earpiece, it was a revolutionary concept. The small device sat in her ear and allowed Uhura and others to communicate wirelessly. From Starfleet Technical Manual With her earpiece, Uhura could track and listen to what was going on inside and outside the the ship. Bluetooth from Walmart While the modern Bluetooth may not be used in outer space, it’s capabilities, and the way that it connects to signals is eerily similar to the Star Trek earpiece. You can even purchase a Star Trek inspired Bluetooth today. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: How did Anakin become a Force Ghost in Return of the Jedi?
Answer: Obi-Wan called out to Anakin after he passed away and taught him the ability to become a Force Spirit Fans have wondered for years how exactly Anakin was taught the ability to transcend death and become a Force Ghost. Finally this mystery was revealed in the short story, Brotherhood, from a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi. In the chapter “Brotherhood”, Anakin left his body of Vader and resided in the Living Force. However, instead of dispersing within the Force like most people, Anakin discovered that he kept his individuality, and consciousness actually grew stronger. For a time Anakin alternated between experiencing for the first time in his life true peace and for the first time fighting for his life, not because he wanted to live, but because he wanted to undo all the evil and suffering he had caused. As that happened Anakin heard the voices of his loved ones and finally he gave into the currents he was fighting. After giving in, Skywalker heard the voice of his old Master, Kenobi. Obi-Wan joked with Anakin telling him cause there was no Holonet for the poster boy anymore. Anakin respdonded sourly that he was no hero and then he had done terrible things and taken so many from so many people, including Obi-Wan himself. It was a watershed moment and Anakin began to confess all of his sins to his Old Master. Obi-Wan retorted that none of that mattered and a person is not completely made up of the choices that they make. Anakin responded that he wanted power to save others, but instead he destroyed them. Kenobi reassured Skywalker and told him that he did not make all of those those decisions on his own, and he doesn’t bear the guilt or sins of the galaxy, just his own. But Kenobi said he wanted his old Padawan to understand that the most important decision was the choice to chose life and goodness over death and darkness, that was the real choice and Anakin chose correctly. Kenobi then told Anakin he wanted to show him something. Kenobi transported them to the scene in RotJ, when Luke was burning his body and the party and celebration that followed. Anakin watched his children and their friends with happiness and a smile. Anakin mused on the thought that as a Padawan and a Knight he had always stood alone trying to solve everything for everyone and protect everyone. But he was never actually present in the moment with his loved ones as his children are right now. He realizes that all of his loved ones were always there urging him to let go of his attachments and be in the moment and he had never listened. His misguided beliefs of trying to be a ‘hero’, to be what he assumed others wanted him to be was always his ego. Letting go of attachments wasn’t as much as a physical thing as much as it was an acceptance of who he truly was and he had never considered that. Obi-Wan pointed out that the twins are what was best of who Anakin and Padme were. As Anakin accepted this he realized that he had manifested himself on the physical plane with Obi-Wan. Anakin then realized that he was wearing the Jedi robes a Jedi Master and became embarrassed. He told Obi-Wan it wasn’t intentional on his part, but Kenobi replied that Anakin might not have chosen it, but perhaps it chose him. Anakin then suddenly noticed that Luke was staring at him and could see him and then Anakin really looked at his daughter and realize how much she reminded him of Padme. Yoda suddenly appeared and told Anakin that his children had a hard and uncertain future road ahead of them. Anakin felt the urge (his ego) to try to step in and fix things, but this time he truly let it go. He simply told Yoda and Obi-Wan that he had faith in his children and for the first time ever, Anakin truly let go. That was the final lesson that Anakin had to learn, and he realized that that moment that it was of course, Obi-Wan that gave him the nudge in that direction . And if you wonder why Anakin appeared as his younger self, well that’s because the taint of Vader was gone once Anakin saved the Galaxy. Question: In Star Trek canon why was "1701" chosen for the Enterprise registry number?
Answer: The 17 stood for the fact that the Constitution-class was Starfleet’s 17th starship design and that the Enterprise was the first, 01, Constitution Class to be constructed producing its number 1701 The USS Constitution was the prototype, therefore its designation was NCC-1700. Since it was the first Constitution Class starship, its registry number was 0, hence the 1700. The U.S.S. Enterprise was the first produced Constitution Class starship built after the original and therefore had the registry number 1701. In canon I don’t think there was ever an explanation what NCC stood for. Matt Jefferies, the artist and set designer for the original series, gave a much more practical and mundane reason for the 1701 designation. “The one seven zero part - I needed a number that would be instantly identifiable, and three, six, eight and nine are too easily confused. I don’t think anyone’ll confuse a one and a seven, or the zero.” -Matt Jefferies Matt Jefferies 1701 was also chosen because the numbers were quite distinctive and looked good on the Enterprise’s hull. Eventually, NCC became the prefix for standard ships. NX is the prefix for experimental ships. 1701 became the official Enterprise registry number. Any other Federation Enterprises inherit that number, but with a letter suffix to differentiate. For example, the Enterprise Picard has in TNG is the NCC 1701-D. Reprint of 1975 First Technical Manual authored in 1986 Listing of Original Constitution Class Starships from 1986 Technical Manual I even have a couple of the official Starfleet technical manuals and I think the original one, but it isn’t clear what NCC stands for. I hope that clears up any confusion! I💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Do orcas ever sink boats?
Answer: Yes, and what’s worrisome as it seems that the amount and the frequency of those attacks are increasing Since 2020, there have been over 100 'interactions' where boats have been spun around, pushed, rammed, or damaged. According to Marine Industry UK, initially scientists identified three culprits. Reports of aggressive encounters with orcas off the Iberian coast began in May 2020 and are becoming more frequent, according to a study published June 2022 in the journal Marine Mammal Science. Assaults seem to be mainly directed at sailing boats and follow a clear pattern, with orcas approaching from the stern to strike the rudder, then losing interest once they have successfully stopped the boat By 2022, however, the number is up to 17 individual Orcas who have participated in the attacks. One such attack in 2020 was experienced by: “Ester Kristine Storkson was asleep on her father's small yacht earlier this month, sailing off the coast of France, when she was violently awakened.” “Scrambling on deck, she spotted several orcas, or killer whales, surrounding them. The steering wheel swung wildly. At one point, the 37-foot sailboat was pushed through 180 degrees, heading it in the opposite direction.” “They were "ramming the boat," Storkson says. "They [hit] us repeatedly ... giving us the impression that it was a coordinated attack." “After about 15 minutes, the orcas broke off, leaving father and daughter to assess the damage. They stuck a GoPro camera in the water, she says, and could see that "approximately three-quarters of [the rudder] was broken off, and some metal was bent." Source: Killer Whales are attacking boats and scientists don’t know why Also in 2020, in one day Orcas sunk one boat in Portugal and severely damaged, another one badly enough that it had to be towed back to dry dock. Source: Orca attacks in Portugal Recently in 2023, Orca attacks have been increasing. Orcas have attacked and sank three sailboats off the coast of Spain and Morocco, attacked many more. Experts suspect that a female orca they call White Gladis suffered a "critical moment of agony" — a collision with a boat or entrapment during illegal fishing — that flipped a behavioral switch. "That traumatized orca is the one that started this behavior of physical contact with the boat," López Fernandez said.” Source: Frequent Orca attacks Orcas are social creatures that can easily learn and reproduce behaviors performed by others, according to the 2022 study. In the majority of reported cases, orcas have made a beeline for a boat's rudder and either bitten, bent or broken it. Scientists think a traumatized orca initiated the assault on boats after a "critical moment of agony" and that the behavior is spreading among the population through social learning. Orcas have attacked and sunk a third boat off the Iberian coast of Europe, and experts now believe the behavior is being copied by the rest of the population. “Three orcas (Orcinus orca), also known as killer whales, struck the yacht on the night of May 4 in the Strait of Gibraltar, off the coast of Spain, and pierced the rudder. "There were two smaller and one larger orca," skipper Werner Schaufelberger told the German publication Yacht. "The little ones shook the rudder at the back while the big one repeatedly backed up and rammed the ship with full force from the side." Schaufelberger said he saw the smaller orcas imitate the larger one. "The two little orcas observed the bigger one's technique and, with a slight run-up, they too slammed into the boat." Spanish coast guards rescued the crew and towed the boat to Barbate, but it sank at the port entrance. Source: Orcas sink three boats in Europe recently Two days earlier, a pod of six orcas assailed another sailboat navigating the strait. Greg Blackburn, who was aboard the vessel, looked on as a mother orca appeared to teach her calf how to charge into the rudder. "It was definitely some form of education, teaching going on," Blackburn told 9news. The spike in aggression towards boats is a recent phenomenon, López Fernandez said. Researchers think that a traumatic event may have triggered a change in the behavior of one orca, which the rest of the population has learned to imitate. “The orcas are doing this on purpose, of course, we don't know the origin or the motivation, but defensive behavior based on trauma, as the origin of all this, gains more strength for us every day," López Fernandez said.” Source: Supra So in conclusion, yes, Orcas do attack and sink ships and have done so with frequent consistency. Question: What moments in Star Trek left us feeling heartbroken?

The conversation they had together was incredibly beautiful, sad and tragic. It was a wonderfully beautiful scene in which two men who had been best friends, more like brothers, spent their final moments together. Mr. Spock, admitted in his dying moments, that he had never faced a no win scenario (the exact scenario Mr. Spock never experienced since he never took the Kobayashi Maru test). But without hesitation, Mr. Spock gave his life, fully knowing that he was going to die, to save the lives of his friends, family, and the entire crew of the Enterprise. Mr. Spock so eloquently stated that the needs of the many outweighed the needs of the few..or the one. If there is any scene in Star Trek that made me cry, this was it. The City on the Edge of Forever Another moment in Star Trek that left me heartbroken was from the original series episode, “The City on the Edge of Forever.” In this tragic story, Bones, Spock and Kirk get transported back in time to New York City during the Great Depression. The three of them are mistaken as homeless, and are taken in by the empathetic and forward thinking Edith Keeler. Edith Keeler and James Tiberius Kirk After Keeler helps the trio, she and Kirk quickly fall in love. unfortunately, Mr. Spock uncovers that Keeler is the subject of a timeline shift and is supposed to die in a car accident. Alternative Timeline in which Keeler lives When the moment comes for Kirk to decide, it's fast and brutal. Kirk is so distraught and heartbroken by the loss of Edith that he even ignores the Guardian of Forever's invitations for other journeys through time. The last line is Kirk's resigned sigh of "Let's get the hell out of here." The Paradise Syndrome Another episode that left me heartbroken again from the original series was from the episode, entitled The Paradise Syndrome. Captain Kirk is a ladies man, but time after time again, when James actually finds a true relationship or falls in love, and is truly happy, that happiness is always plucked away from him and ends in tragedy. McCoy and Mr. Spock show in the nick of time and safely rescue Kirk, but they are unable to save Miramanee. She and their child dies in Kirk’s arms. Kirk had never had a relationship with his son until the events of Star Trek II. The two finally found common ground and a budding relationship was forming between Father and Son. Just before his death, David and James had expressed their love and affection for each other and buried the hatchet. David let go of any feelings of animosity he had fostered over the years. Vader also became the greatest light saber duelist of all time surpassing Sidious in that respect as well. Even though he desperately wanted revenge against his old master, Vader stayed the course and listened to his master and slaughtered any remaining Jedi he could find. Vader was the hand and will of the Emperor. A battlefield commander who led his troops from the front and feared nothing. Vader killed at least 30 Jedi after order 66. Even Maul did everything he could to avoid a direct confrontation with Vader because he knew he would lose. Vader surpassed Anakin and his anger and rage helped him to become the most powerful Sith of all time. Vader himself recognized the culmination in what he had become. His failure came because his love for his son unbalanced his soul and his emotional state and ruined his perfected state of pure rage and hatred. Vader’s son Luke used The Darkside in connection with Form v to defeated his emotionally conflicted father in ROTJ. Question: How exactly did LaForge restore the Enterprise D? Did he salvage the rest of the ship or just replicate it?
Answer: LaForge used the intact saucer section and reattached it to the rebuilt hull The Enterprise NCC-1701-D was so badly damaged that it crashed landed on the surface of Veridian III. The Saucer section of the Enterprise remained intact while there was substantial damage done to the hull and the rest of the ship. The Federation feared that inhabitants of its neighboring planets may have recovered it in violation of the Prime Directive so the Saucer section was brought back to the Federation Fleet Musuem. It was transported to the Fleet Museum. In Generations, Data said the neighboring planet, Verdian IV, had a “pre-industrial society.” meaning that just the presence of advanced technology from Starfleet in a burgeoning star system necessitated removing that said technology. Geordi had been appointed Commodore of the Fleet Musuem and secretly worked on restoring the Enterprise-D which he kept hidden in docking bay 12 of the Fleet Museum. In Episode 9, Geordi revealed that he had fully restored the Enterprise-D. LaForge explained that since the Saucer was intact, he had been spending the last 20 years repairing the rest of the ship using spare parts. LaForge revealed that he cannibalized engines and nacelles from the U.S.S. Syracuse and other ships. Geordi must’ve replaced the entire drive section (for the engineering section for example) from another Galaxy-Class Starship. And other parts as he needed. This means that roughly, LaForge had been working on restoring Enterprise-D since the end of the events of Nemesis in 2379. The entire company were astounded to see the NCC-1701-D flying again, none moreso than Admiral Picard. So in conclusion, LaForge cannibalized, and used spare parts, from other, retired Starships from the Fleet museum to restore Enterprise-D to working order. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: In Star Wars, what standard year was the Ultimate weapon called the Death Star? And what Star Wars character named it?

Though the concept of a mobile planet destroying battle station super weapon was actually originally thought about and designed almost 1000 years before during the time of the ancient Sith. The Geonosians along with Dooku and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, designed the original Death Star 1 and began to build the terrifying planet killer before the year 22 BBY. The plans for the DS-1 were moved from the Geonosians and given to Sidious by Lord Tyrannus. Question: Do any alien species in Star Wars have innate powers and abilities?
Answer: Many alien species do but I’m going to discuss one of my favorites from Legends, the Ysalamir (and the force sensitive non sentient being the Vornskr) Ysalamiri Ysalamiri were lizard-like tree-dwellers about 50 centimeters in length native to the planet Myrkr, most known for their ability to repel the Force by creating a Force-neutral bubble. This ability evolved in response to predation by the Force-sensitive vornskrs. Vornskr The vornskr were a canine beast that could hunt using the Force. Vornskrs were native to the forest planet Myrkr and hunted the native ysalamiri. Over time, the ysalamiri developed abilities to suppress the Force as a defensive adaptation against vornskrs. Many ysalamiri grouped together would expand their Force-neutral bubble by varying distances—sometimes by kilometers. The ysalamiri to me were always a truly fascinating nonsentient creature. They made their debut in the Timothy Zahn Heir to the Empire trilogy. Grand Admiral Thrawn discovered them and used them to protect himself and select troops from Force wielding beings albeit Jedi, Sith or crazed clones like Joruus C’baoth. Clone of Joruus C’baoth The ysalamiri did not negate the force, because that would stand in opposition to what Yoda said that all existence was infused with Force energy. Instead the ysalamiri projected a bubble inside which users were unable to exert any influence over the Force. A single ysalamiri could produce a bubble that measured up to 10 meters in diameter. Groupings of ysalamiri could combine their ability and could extend their bubble to much greater distances up to kilometers in size. Zahn introduced a ton of memorable and amazing characters like Mara Jade and creatures like the ysalamiri. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questi, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: How old is Romania?
Answer: Romania has been settled and occupied at least since 35,000 B.C. Skull of inhabitant of Romania circa 35,000 B.C. Romania history is a long and interesting one. Evidence of modern humans have been found in modern day Romania dating back to 34,950 B.C. Neolithic Romania The Neolithic period of ancient Romania lasted from 10.000 BC to 2000 BC. The Neolithic people were indigenous Europeans who were later conquered by the Indo-Europeans. The indigenous people of Neolithic cultures from present-day Romania are believed to have mixed with Proto-Indo-Europeans, giving birth to proto-Thracians from which Thracians and Dacians developed later on. Thracians The intermixing of Indo-Europeans and these Neolithic farmers became known as Thracians. These Thracians first settled in the Danube-Carthpathian region of Romania. The area transformed into the Kingdom of Dacia by Burebista (c. 80-44 B.C.), who conquered and united several other Dacian principalities. Dacia under Burebista The Dacians had periods of independence and were also controlled by invading forces such as the Celts, Persians and eventually came into conflict with the Roman Empire. Dacia was an independent kingdom that Rome had long desired. Several campaigns were launched against the Independent Kingdom but none were completely successful. Rome greatly desired the bountiful amount of salt which was plentiful in Dacia. Salt was a necessity in the ancient world because it helped preserve meat and fish in a world before refrigerators. Salt was incredibly plentiful in Dacia so much that there are salt mines even there today. Many people incorrectly believe Dacia was invaded because of its gold but Rome only discovered the copious amounts of the precious metal after their invasion by accident. When the Romans decisively attacked Dacia, the locals hid this lucrative treasure in a riverbed by diverting the river from its course. The Romans only happened upon this fortune years later. The Dacians often entered Roman territory and plundered wherever they went. Eventually the Roman Emperor Trajen launched two military campaigns against Dacia that were ultimately successful in 101-102 and 105-106 A.D. Campaign of Dacia by the Emperor Trajan Trajan and his legions crushed the forces of Dacia and completely occupied the kingdom. To stamp out any attempt at rebellion, the Romans made slaves of the population of Dacia and sent them to the far corners of the Empire. As history reveals, the policy of the Romans was to colonize every foreign country they had conquered by war in order that the conquest might last and a further expansion of the Roman Empire be possible. This policy was also followed by Trajan with the Dacians by colonizing their land with Roman soldiers and Roman officials. In fact, the entire administration of Dacia was Roman. Besides the Roman legions and officials, another element came to Dacia: Roman merchants who usually followed their armies. The Kingdom of Dacia was completely changed linguistically and ethnically. Most of the modern day Romanians can trace their heritage to a mixture of Roman and Thracian culture and peoples. This is why the Romanian language is a Romance language because it originates from Vulgar Latin, which is a subgroup of the Italic branch of the Indo-European language family. The Romans eventually abandoned Dacia in 271 A.D. when they grew tired of fighting the rebellious Dacians and the barbaric Goths who invaded the province from the east. Marcus Aurelius decided to abandon Dacia completely. I won’t go into the history of modern day Romania after the Romans abandoned the Territory Because it would make this answer way too long.
